sources.title: On Citizenship of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The official legislation portal identifies the citizenship law as in force and displays its current revision history.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Law of Ukraine on January 18, 2001 No. 2235-III

sources.title: Acquisition of Ukrainian Citizenship
sources.officialityEvidence: The current State Migration Service page identifies a passport for travel abroad as a document confirming Ukrainian citizenship.
sources.supportingExcerpt: passport of the citizen of Ukraine for travelling abroad

sources.title: MFA resumes issuing electronic visas (e-Visa) to foreigners
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The official MFA notice records operational e-Visa resumption on 19 February 2025, but its 45-country eligibility statement conflicts with the 43-state page recorded as ukraine-mfa-evisa-43-states.
sources.supportingExcerpt: resumes issuing electronic visas (e-Visa) to foreigners

sources.title: e-Visa
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA e-Visa page describes eligibility for 43 states, conflicting with ukraine-mfa-evisa-resumption-2025's 45-country statement; the page returned 403 during this review and is risk evidence only.

sources.title: Entry regime to Ukraine for foreign citizens
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA page identifies its nationality table as of 8 June 2023; it returned 403 during this review, so it is recorded only as stale/inaccessible evidence risk.

sources.title: Extending the duration of stay on the territory of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The current State Migration Service guidance distinguishes visa-based stays from visa-free 90-in-180 stays without publishing a nationality schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: visa-free entry regime may stay temporarily ... up to 90 days during any 180 day period

sources.title: The Ministry of Internal Affairs has developed an algorithm of actions on the entry and stay of foreigners
sources.publisher: Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry describes entry documentation and conduct under martial law but does not publish nationality-specific visa categories.
sources.supportingExcerpt: taking into account the introduction of martial law in Ukraine

policies.title: Ukrainian ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Ukrainian ordinary-passport traveller is classified as citizenship, not as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: This is a narrow catalogue home classification. Martial-law restrictions, military records, dual nationality, residence, work and special-document rules are outside the ordinary foreign-visitor baseline.
